web.title: AI Tutors Can Work—With the Right Guardrails | Edutopia
web.description:
But AI, it turns out, _can_ be a useful tutor—if it’s designed and deployed with the proper guardrails.

The researchers provided the AI with “teacher input on common student mistakes and how to provide feedback,” and prompted it to “provide hints to the student without directly giving them the answer.”

## The Principal Project helps you navigate the daily realities of leadership.
### How to Create an AI Tutor
As Khan Academy [shows in its demo](https://www.khanacademy.org/college-careers-more/khanmigo-for-students/x5443352261243283:introducing-khanmigo/x5443352261243283:getting-started-with-khanmigo/v/khanmigo-for-students-what-is-khanmigo-and-how-does-it-work), both have been designed not to give students the answers.

This sample interaction shows that when a chatbot is prompted to take on the role of a tutor, it can help guide students toward an in-depth understanding of specific class material without giving the answers away.
